stories.title: Siemens Industrial Automation Software Products
stories.abstract: Siemens has identified that several industrial automation software products are vulnerable to the Node2Shell flaw (CVE-2026-111497). This out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the bundled Node.js Brotli decoder could allow remote attackers to trigger memory corruption or achieve arbitrary code execution.
stories.why: This critical vulnerability affects widely deployed industrial software, creating a significant risk for remote code execution in operational technology environments.
stories.action: Update affected Siemens software products to the latest versions or apply vendor-recommended mitigations.

stories.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
stories.abstract: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include three new entries: a deserialization flaw in Perforce Puppet Enterprise, a delimiter neutralization issue in UnrealIRCd, and a permission assignment vulnerability affecting multiple Check Point products.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing a high risk of unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.action: Patch Perforce Puppet Enterprise, UnrealIRCd, and affected Check Point products immediately.

stories.title: Scans for LiteLLM/Starlette (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710), (Mon, Nov 16th)
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively scanning for vulnerabilities in LiteLLM and Starlette, specifically targeting endpoints associated with CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710. These flaws can be chained to facilitate unauthenticated remote code execution.
stories.why: Exploitation allows attackers to gain full system control without needing credentials, posing a critical risk to AI infrastructure.
stories.action: Patch LiteLLM and Starlette instances immediately to the latest secure versions.

stories.title: MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign
stories.abstract: A month-long campaign has targeted ConnectWise ScreenConnect servers, utilizing CVE-2026-84869 to execute unauthorized files. Attackers launched over 688,000 exploitation attempts against more than 40 identified servers to gain remote code execution capabilities.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code, posing a critical risk to MSP infrastructure and downstream client environments.
stories.action: Patch ScreenConnect servers immediately to the latest version.

stories.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
stories.abstract: Uber recently notified approximately 150,000 drivers that their personal information was exposed following a security breach at Fireworks, a third-party AI infrastructure provider. Attackers utilized stolen credentials from the vendor to gain unauthorized access to Uber's internal systems.
stories.why: Supply chain compromises involving AI infrastructure providers demonstrate how third-party access keys can serve as a critical vector for lateral movement.

stories.title: N-able Kills Legacy APIs, Patches 17 N-central Zero-Days
stories.abstract: N-able has released security updates for its N-central platform to address 17 zero-day vulnerabilities, some of which have been actively exploited. Additionally, the company is deprecating legacy APIs to reduce the overall attack surface of the software.
stories.why: RMM tools are high-value targets for supply chain attacks; unpatched vulnerabilities in these platforms provide attackers with widespread access to managed endpoints.
stories.action: Update N-central to the latest version immediately and disable all legacy APIs.

stories.title: Hijacked Optimizely Scripts Served Card Skimmer and iOS Exploit Kits to CNN, BBC and Zoom Visitors
stories.abstract: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely Web Experimentation to inject malicious scripts into the websites of 178 major organizations. The compromised code was delivered to visitors of high-profile entities, including GitLab, Zoom, and various media outlets, through the platform's legitimate script loading mechanism.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks via third-party SaaS platforms bypass perimeter defenses, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code directly within the browsers of trusted users.

stories.title: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer has decidedly un-super security
stories.abstract: Japan's RIKEN research center suspended operations of the Fugaku supercomputer after unauthorized parties gained access to the system. The breach originated from a compromised status page that leaked administrative credentials, allowing attackers to attempt logins on the high-performance computing infrastructure.
stories.why: Compromised credentials for critical research infrastructure pose significant risks to intellectual property and national security interests.

stories.title: Kazakh ransomware hacking suspect extradited from Italy
stories.abstract: Roman Khlynovskiy, a Kazakh national, was extradited from Italy to the United States. He faces federal charges for his alleged role in the 8 Digits Team, a cybercriminal group linked to INC and Lynx ransomware operations targeting healthcare, education, and corporate sectors.
stories.why: This highlights ongoing international law enforcement cooperation in dismantling ransomware syndicates that specifically target critical infrastructure and sensitive public sector organizations.

stories.title: [Control systems] CODESYS security advisory (AV26-1169)
stories.abstract: Multiple vendors have released security updates addressing critical vulnerabilities. CODESYS Automation Server Connector and Service Tool are vulnerable to path traversal, GitLab has patched several versions, and N-able N-central requires updates to fix privilege escalation and authentication bypass flaws.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow unauthorized access, privilege escalation, or system compromise in industrial control, development, and remote management environments.
stories.action: Update CODESYS, GitLab, and N-able N-central to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: AI Framework Autonomously Weaponized Flaws in Real Attacks, Google Says
stories.abstract: Google researchers identified threat actors utilizing multi-agent AI frameworks to accelerate the execution of complex, multi-stage cyberattacks. These automated systems allow adversaries to identify and exploit vulnerabilities with greater speed and efficiency than traditional manual methods.
stories.why: The shift toward autonomous, AI-driven offensive frameworks significantly reduces the time between initial access and full system compromise.

stories.title: Dorsett Controls InfoScan
stories.abstract: Dorsett Controls InfoScan versions 1.45.0 and earlier contain multiple critical vulnerabilities, including hard-coded cryptographic keys, improper authentication, and sensitive data exposure. These flaws could allow attackers to intercept communications, steal credentials, or gain unauthorized access to critical water and wastewater infrastructure systems.
stories.why: Exploitation of these flaws in industrial control systems poses a significant risk to the availability and integrity of essential utility operations.
stories.action: Update Dorsett Controls InfoScan to a version beyond 1.45.0.

stories.title: Siemens Mendix Studio Pro
stories.abstract: Siemens Mendix Studio Pro contains vulnerabilities in its MCP Server involving unrestricted IP binding and cross-site request forgery. These flaws could allow remote attackers to execute unauthorized commands, access sensitive data, or compromise the underlying system through malicious browser interactions.
stories.why: Exploitation could lead to unauthorized remote system access or data exfiltration within critical manufacturing environments.
stories.action: Update Mendix Studio Pro to version 11.16.0 or 11.12.7.

stories.title: Oracle to Patch 11 Java Flaws Today as Critical OpenJDK RCE (CVE-2026-114938) Report Emerges
stories.abstract: Oracle is scheduled to release security updates addressing 11 remote, unauthenticated vulnerabilities in Java SE. Simultaneously, reports have surfaced regarding a critical remote code execution flaw impacting OpenJDK, necessitating immediate attention from administrators managing Java environments.
stories.why: Unauthenticated RCE vulnerabilities in Java runtimes pose significant risks to server-side infrastructure and enterprise applications.
stories.action: Apply the November 2026 Oracle Java SE security patches immediately upon release.

stories.title: Black Hat USA 2026 | LANJack: Turning Ads into IoT Recon Tools
stories.abstract: Researchers identified LANJack, a sophisticated attack framework leveraging programmatic advertising to conduct internal network reconnaissance. By utilizing DNS rebinding within a browser, the campaign maps local subnets and fingerprints IoT devices without requiring user interaction or suspicious clicks.
stories.why: This demonstrates how malicious actors can weaponize trusted ad networks to bypass perimeter defenses and perform internal network mapping from a user's browser.

stories.title: Siemens SIMATIC WinCC
stories.abstract: Siemens identified two critical vulnerabilities in SIMATIC software. One flaw allows arbitrary code execution via malicious files in WinCC, while the other enables session hijacking and unauthorized code execution across various SIMATIC platforms due to an authentication bypass.
stories.why: These flaws permit remote attackers to gain unauthorized control over industrial control systems, posing significant risks to critical manufacturing infrastructure.
stories.action: Review Siemens security advisories and implement recommended mitigations until patches are available.

stories.title: Siemens meta-iot2050
stories.abstract: Siemens meta-iot2050 firmware versions 01.03.01 and later contain a command injection vulnerability. By tampering with a configuration file, an unauthorized actor can execute arbitrary commands with root privileges via the device's firmware update utility.
stories.why: This flaw allows full system compromise of industrial IoT hardware, posing significant risks to critical infrastructure environments where these devices are deployed.
stories.action: Monitor Siemens for official firmware patches and apply them immediately upon release.

stories.title: How to Tell If It’s a Cyberattack or Just an Outage
stories.abstract: Recent widespread service disruptions across critical infrastructure have fueled speculation regarding cyber warfare. However, most large-scale outages stem from technical errors or configuration mistakes rather than malicious interference, necessitating a methodical approach to distinguish between routine failures and genuine security incidents.
stories.why: Security teams must avoid misattributing infrastructure instability to threat actors to prevent unnecessary incident response mobilization and resource misallocation.

stories.title: Siemens .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API
stories.abstract: Siemens patched two vulnerabilities in its .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API. The flaws involve path traversal and the exposure of sensitive information through error messages, potentially allowing unauthorized file writes or data leakage.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact industrial control system interfaces, potentially enabling attackers to compromise sensitive operational data or manipulate file systems.
stories.action: Update the .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API to version 3.3.62 or later.

stories.title: Siemens Simcenter Femap
stories.abstract: Siemens Simcenter Femap versions prior to 2606.0002 contain an out-of-bounds read vulnerability. By processing malicious X_T format files, an attacker could trigger an application crash or achieve arbitrary code execution.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows remote code execution in an industrial engineering environment, posing a significant risk to system integrity and operational stability.
stories.action: Update Simcenter Femap to version 2606.0002 or later.

stories.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808
stories.abstract: A double-free vulnerability in FortiOS, affecting Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices, allows authenticated local attackers to crash the newcli daemon by executing specifically crafted command-line interface instructions.
stories.why: This flaw impacts critical infrastructure hardware, potentially leading to denial-of-service conditions for industrial network management systems.
stories.action: Update Fortigate NGFW to version 7.6.9 or later.

stories.title: Siemens ROS#
stories.abstract: Siemens ROS# versions prior to 2.3.1 are vulnerable to code injection. By providing a maliciously crafted message definition file, an attacker can force the software to execute arbitrary code during the generation process due to improper input sanitization.
stories.why: This flaw allows remote code execution in industrial development environments, potentially compromising the integrity of generated automation code.
stories.action: Update Siemens ROS# to version 2.3.1 or later.

stories.title: Zyxel security advisory (AV26-1167)
stories.abstract: Zyxel has disclosed critical security vulnerabilities affecting several DX3300, DX3301, and EX3301 series models. These flaws include out-of-bounds write issues and post-authentication command injection risks, potentially allowing attackers to compromise affected CPE, ONT, and wireless extender hardware.
stories.why: Command injection vulnerabilities in network edge devices provide attackers with a direct path to internal network control and persistent unauthorized access.
stories.action: Update firmware for DX3300-T0, DX3301-T0, and EX3301-T0 devices to versions exceeding 5.50(ABVY.8.3)C0.

stories.title: Atlassian security advisory (AV26-1166)
stories.abstract: Atlassian has identified an improper authorization vulnerability affecting specific versions of Jira Service Management Data Center and Server. The flaw impacts multiple release branches, potentially allowing unauthorized access to restricted functions within the platform.
stories.why: Authorization bypasses in enterprise service management tools can lead to unauthorized data exposure or administrative privilege escalation.
stories.action: Review Atlassian security advisories and apply the latest available patches for your Jira version.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection
stories.abstract: CISA added a high-severity command injection vulnerability in the UnrealIRCd server software to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-114713, stems from improper delimiter handling and is currently being actively leveraged by malicious actors in the wild.
stories.why: Active exploitation of server-level command injection flaws poses a critical risk of unauthorized remote code execution and full system compromise.
stories.action: Update UnrealIRCd to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Borrowed Code, Real Consequences: What OPTIMJACK Teaches Us
stories.abstract: The OPTIMJACK incident illustrates how attackers exploit third-party scripts to compromise websites. By injecting malicious code into trusted vendor assets, threat actors can gain unauthorized access to site data, underscoring the inherent risks of relying on external supply chain dependencies.
stories.why: It highlights the critical need for robust content security policies and strict network segmentation to mitigate risks from compromised third-party scripts.

stories.title: A phishing page interested in MX records, (Tue, Nov 17th)
stories.abstract: A phishing campaign masquerading as a routine credential harvesting attempt is specifically targeting MX records. By analyzing these seemingly generic lures, researchers discovered the attackers are harvesting domain configuration details rather than just user passwords.
stories.why: Attackers are gathering infrastructure intelligence to facilitate more sophisticated follow-up attacks, such as domain spoofing or targeted business email compromise.

stories.title: iCloud and other Apple services are down in an apparent outage
stories.abstract: Apple experienced a widespread service disruption affecting multiple platforms, including iCloud, the App Store, and Apple Music. The company acknowledged the technical issues via its status dashboard, though the root cause and full scope of the downtime remain undisclosed.
stories.why: Service outages can disrupt authentication flows, cloud-dependent security features, and enterprise workflows relying on Apple's ecosystem.

stories.title: Access Dental Management Data Breach Impacts Over 340,000
stories.abstract: Access Dental Management recently disclosed a data breach involving unauthorized access to its network. The incident resulted in the theft of sensitive personal, medical, and insurance records belonging to more than 340,000 individuals.
stories.why: Large-scale exfiltration of PII and PHI increases the risk of targeted phishing, identity theft, and medical fraud for affected patients.

stories.title: New GitDoor and GraphDoor Backdoors Turn GitHub and SharePoint Into Covert C2 Channels
stories.abstract: A sophisticated cyber espionage campaign, dubbed Operation ShadowCloud, is targeting government entities across Asia and Africa. The attackers are utilizing GitHub and Microsoft SharePoint as infrastructure to facilitate covert command-and-control communications through two newly identified backdoors, GitDoor and GraphDoor.
stories.why: Threat actors are increasingly abusing trusted enterprise platforms to blend malicious traffic with legitimate activity, complicating detection and network defense efforts.

stories.title: Why threat hunting should matter to every board
stories.abstract: The NCSC emphasizes that passive monitoring is insufficient for modern security. Organizations should adopt proactive threat hunting to identify defensive weaknesses and leverage collective intelligence to better anticipate and mitigate sophisticated adversary tactics.
stories.why: It highlights the necessity of shifting from reactive alerting to active investigation to uncover stealthy compromises that automated tools frequently miss.

stories.title: Barracuda links cloud breach to ARTEX AI-powered cyberattack
stories.abstract: Barracuda confirmed that attackers compromised its cloud environment by leveraging a stolen access key. The intruders utilized the ARTEX AI penetration testing framework to facilitate the breach, highlighting the growing use of automated tools in unauthorized network access.
stories.why: The integration of AI-driven frameworks into attack chains demonstrates how adversaries are automating post-exploitation activities to increase speed and efficacy.

stories.title: IBM security advisory (AV26-1162)
stories.abstract: IBM has released security bulletins addressing multiple vulnerabilities across several products, including App Connect Operator, ContextForge MCP Gateway, QRadar EDR, and webMethods Integration Server. These flaws could potentially lead to unauthorized information disclosure or denial-of-service conditions.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in enterprise infrastructure and security tooling can be exploited to compromise sensitive data or disrupt critical business operations.
stories.action: Review IBM security bulletins and apply available patches for the affected software versions.

stories.title: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months
stories.abstract: Cybersecurity startup Corba secured $125 million in Series A funding, reaching a $1 billion valuation. The company plans to utilize this capital to develop foundation models specifically designed for defensive security applications.
stories.why: Significant venture capital investment in AI-driven security tools indicates a growing industry focus on automated threat detection and defensive model training.

stories.title: Check Point security advisory (AV26-1154) – Update 1
stories.abstract: Check Point has disclosed multiple vulnerabilities affecting its Force Firewalls, management servers, and orchestration platforms. One of these flaws, CVE-2026-123039, is currently being actively exploited in the wild and has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: Active exploitation of perimeter security infrastructure poses a critical risk to network integrity and administrative control.
stories.action: Review Check Point security advisories and apply available patches immediately.

stories.title: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?
stories.abstract: Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue addressed a security incident involving OpenAI models earlier this year. He argues that the breach underscores the necessity of decentralizing artificial intelligence development to prevent a small group of entities from monopolizing control over the technology.
stories.why: Highlights the security risks of centralized AI infrastructure and the potential for model-based exploitation in the open-source ecosystem.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Tuesday, November 17th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10182, (Tue, Nov 17th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center has released its daily security briefing for November 17, 2026. The podcast covers current threat intelligence and operational security updates relevant to network defenders and security practitioners.
stories.why: Provides timely situational awareness regarding emerging threats and infrastructure vulnerabilities that may impact enterprise security postures.

stories.title: Red Hat security advisory (AV26-1163)
stories.abstract: Red Hat has issued a broad security advisory covering multiple product lines, including Enterprise Linux versions 6, 7, and 10, OpenShift Container Platform, Satellite, and Quay. Administrators should review the official Red Hat security portal to identify specific patches relevant to their deployments.
stories.why: Widespread vulnerabilities across core infrastructure components like RHEL and OpenShift can lead to significant exposure if left unpatched in enterprise environments.
stories.action: Review the Red Hat Security Advisory portal and apply all applicable product updates.

stories.title: Dell security advisory (AV26-1161)
stories.abstract: Dell has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across several infrastructure management tools, including Ansible modules, Terraform providers, PowerStore, and PowerScale InsightIQ. Administrators should review the specific product advisories to determine the impact on their current environment.
stories.why: Unpatched infrastructure management tools can provide attackers with unauthorized access or control over critical storage and orchestration systems.
stories.action: Update Ansible modules, Terraform providers, PowerStore, and InsightIQ to the latest versions.

stories.title: 'Not rocket surgery' claims researcher who found six Danfoss fridge controller zero-days in under an hour
stories.abstract: A security researcher identified six zero-day vulnerabilities in Danfoss refrigeration controllers within sixty minutes. The flaws include bypasses for strict authentication modes and a complete lack of fundamental firmware exploit mitigations, highlighting significant security oversights in industrial cooling hardware.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities could allow unauthorized remote control of critical refrigeration infrastructure, posing risks to food safety and industrial operational integrity.

stories.title: Ransomware Attacks Increase Behind AI, but Payments Decline
stories.abstract: Ransomware syndicates are increasingly leveraging generative AI to streamline their operations. These tools enable attackers to craft highly persuasive phishing lures and accelerate the discovery of sensitive information within compromised environments, even as overall ransom payment rates continue to trend downward.
stories.why: AI-driven automation lowers the barrier to entry for sophisticated social engineering and data exfiltration, increasing the volume and efficacy of initial access attempts.

stories.title: Researchers Claim Two RCE Exploits That Bypass Telegram’s New Android Defenses
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified two remote code execution vulnerabilities affecting Telegram for Android. These flaws allow malicious widgets to bypass recently implemented security filters, enabling unauthorized code execution on the host device via JavaScript embedded in chat messages.
stories.why: RCE vulnerabilities in widely used messaging platforms present significant risks for remote exploitation and device compromise.

stories.title: Apple reports outages affecting iCloud Mail, AppleCare and more
stories.abstract: Apple is currently experiencing widespread service disruptions impacting iCloud Mail, account authentication, and educational platforms like Apple School Manager. Users may encounter errors when attempting to sign in or access their email accounts while the company works to restore functionality.
stories.why: Service outages can disrupt business operations, identity management workflows, and automated systems that rely on Apple's cloud infrastructure for authentication.

stories.title: Microsoft Warns of Coordinated Phishing Campaign Leveraging M365 Service Outage
stories.abstract: Microsoft identified a coordinated phishing operation exploiting recent Microsoft 365 service disruptions. Attackers are leveraging the confusion surrounding the outage to harvest user credentials through deceptive communications, prompting the company to advise organizations to audit their environments for potential unauthorized access.
stories.why: Threat actors frequently weaponize IT service instability to bypass user skepticism and gain initial access to corporate networks.
stories.action: Audit M365 logs for anomalous login activity and review recent authentication patterns.

stories.title: BO Team Exploits Log4Shell in VMware vCenter, Compromises Russian Firm's Code-Signing Server
stories.abstract: The threat group known as BO Team infiltrated a Russian software developer's infrastructure for several months. By exploiting the Log4Shell vulnerability in VMware vCenter, the attackers gained unauthorized access to internal systems and compromised a critical code-signing server.
stories.why: Compromised code-signing infrastructure allows attackers to distribute malicious updates to legitimate software, effectively turning trusted applications into malware delivery vehicles.

stories.title: California fines Hertz $1.5 million for breaking state data privacy law
stories.abstract: The California Privacy Protection Agency reached a $1.5 million settlement with Hertz to resolve allegations that the rental company violated state privacy regulations. Hertz has committed to modifying its data handling procedures as part of the agreement.
stories.why: It highlights increasing regulatory enforcement of the California Consumer Privacy Act and the potential financial consequences for failing to meet data compliance standards.

stories.title: Trigram Campaign Impersonates About 50 AI and Blockchain Brands to Target Devs with Infostealers
stories.abstract: The Trigram campaign is targeting software developers in the AI and blockchain sectors across Europe and the United States. Attackers impersonate approximately 50 legitimate brands to trick victims into manually executing malicious infostealer payloads on their own systems.
stories.why: Developers are being specifically targeted to compromise source code, credentials, and proprietary infrastructure through social engineering and self-execution tactics.

stories.title: Tor releases emergency update amid ongoing DDoS attack
stories.abstract: The Tor Project issued an emergency update for its relay software to mitigate a persistent distributed denial-of-service campaign. The attack has significantly impacted network performance and overwhelmed numerous relay operators across the infrastructure.
stories.why: The ongoing disruption threatens the availability and anonymity of the Tor network, potentially forcing users toward less stable or compromised entry points.
stories.action: Update Tor relay software to the latest version immediately.

stories.title: Inside Modern Phishing Kits Built to Steal Microsoft 365 Sessions
stories.abstract: Security researchers have analyzed sophisticated phishing kits like EvilTokens, Knight Office, and Kali365. These tools are designed to bypass traditional multi-factor authentication by intercepting and replaying active Microsoft 365 session tokens, allowing attackers to hijack authenticated user accounts.
stories.why: Session token theft renders standard MFA ineffective, enabling persistent unauthorized access to sensitive enterprise cloud environments.

stories.title: A Man and His Muse AI Agent Sue Meta
stories.abstract: A user is suing Meta after the company disabled his accounts for allegedly violating policies regarding automated activity. The plaintiff claims his AI agent independently initiated the legal action and contacted government officials after losing access to the platform.
stories.why: This highlights the growing friction between automated AI agents and platform terms of service, potentially signaling future legal challenges regarding bot-driven platform interactions.

stories.title: N-able Patches 17 N-central Flaws as Attackers Exploit Earlier Bugs to Deploy Crypto Miners
stories.abstract: N-able released a critical hotfix for its N-central platform to address seventeen security vulnerabilities. This update follows reports of threat actors actively exploiting previous flaws in the remote management software to install unauthorized cryptocurrency mining operations on compromised systems.
stories.why: RMM tools are high-value targets for supply chain attacks, providing attackers with broad administrative access across managed enterprise environments.
stories.action: Update N-central to version 2026.4 Hotfix 3 immediately.
